Faculty of Mathematics and Natural SciencesPhD Student Position (f/m/x) in “Quantum Hall calorimetry of quantum materials“Institute of Physics II | Bocquillon Working GroupWe are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.One PhD Student position is available in the group of Professor Erwann Bocquillon, which specializes in the quantum transport of quantum materials(https://ph2.uni-koeln.de/en/research-groups/bocquillon).The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz - LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, personal orientation and identity.The position is available from 1 January 2027 on a part-time basis (29,87 hours per week).The position is to be filled for a fixed term until 31 December 2029. If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.Please apply online with proof of the required qualifications without a photo via the apply button. The reference number is Wiss2610-07. The application deadline is 30 November 2026.For further inquiries, please contact Professor Dr Erwann Bocquillon (bocquillon@ph2.uni-koeln.de) (scientific part) or Dr Matteo Cacco (cacco@ph2.uni-koeln.de) (application questions) and take a look at our FAQs. YOUR TASKSThis PhD project will develop a new ultra-sensitive quantum calorimeter to explore how heat flows through exotic quantum materials. By combining layered crystals with quantum Hall devices, the researcher will be able to probe elusive states of matter with unprecedented precision-starting with alpha-RuCl3, a leading candidate for hosting Majorana-like particles and a quantum spin liquid. The project offers an opportunity to build new cutting-edge techniques in collaboration with partners at the University of Tokyo (Japan), while tackling some exciting open questions in condensed-matter physics.YOUR PROFILEThe candidate should possess an excellent academic record and hold a Masters in Physics, preferably with a major in Quantum Physics or Condensed Matter Physics. Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA BiologyThe Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience. This work is supported by extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure.Tackling critical questions on PTB functions in A. thaliana using a multidisciplinary approach, which integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, and plant stress physiologyApplying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biologyDeveloping an integrated framework to decipher PTB’s role in splicing and its downstream physiological outcomes, with a particular focus on drought stressAssisting with lab organisation and other general tasksContributing to teaching activities for Bachelor's and Master's students within our groupSupervising PhD students and other group membersPresenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscriptsA successfully completed scientific university degree in Biology or in a related fieldA successfully completed doctorate (PhD) in molecular plant biology or RNA biologyExperience with a spectrum of molecular methodsExperience in plant (stress) physiology is a plus, but not mandatoryTeaching experience is a plus, but not mandatoryVery good English language skills (at least level B2); German language skills are a plus, but not mandatoryA successful academic track record documented by publications, conference contributions, etc.A fascination for science, very good communication and teamwork skillsIn addition to the general requirements according to public services law, applicants must meet the recruitment requirements stipulated in § 57 of the Hochschulgesetz of ...

jobs.occupation: Senior Global Pricing and Access Manager Immuno-Oncology (m/w/d) (Leiter/in - Marketing)
jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: OUR COMPANYAt Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.The PositionAt Boehringer Ingelheim, we are committed to delivering breakthrough therapies that have an unprecedented impact for people facing cancer, today and for generations to come. This high-impact global role contributes to our early oncology pipeline, where payer confidence, evidence quality, development and launch sequencing, and pricing strategy can shape how quickly innovation reaches patients. As (Senior) Global Pricing and Access Manager, you will help define the access ambition for early pipeline products and translate science, payer expectations, competitive dynamics and country realities into clear strategic choices. You will work closely with Global Access, HEOR, Medical, Clinical Development, Regulatory, Commercial, Forecasting, Finance, and regional and local teams to ensure payer needs are embedded in evidence generation, value communication, pricing decisions, and launch planning from the beginning.Tasks & responsibilities- In this role, you will drive the development and execution of global pricing and access strategies for early immuno-oncology assets across current and future indications, ensuring payer considerations are integrated into asset and indication planning.- With a focus on value creation, you will develop and refine payer value propositions by translating clinical, economic and market evidence into compelling value narratives.- As part of a cross-functional environment, you will lead payer-relevant evidence planning in partnership with HEOR, Medical and Clinical colleagues, identifying evidence needs, risks and opportunities.- By providing strategic guidance, you will develop global pricing recommendations that support launch planning, lifecycle management, indication expansion and long-term value optimization.- When evaluating market dynamics, you will lead the generation and interpretation of payer, HTA, reimbursement and competitive insights, translating findings into actionable recommendations.- Within your area of responsibility, you will drive access launch readiness across regions and markets, ensuring global strategies and value communications are effectively translated into local implementation.- Through close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will ensure payer and access perspectives are reflected in development, evidence and commercialization planning.Requirements- Graduate degree in Medicine, Life Sciences, Health Economics, Pharmacy, Business, Finance, or a related discipline.- Long term experience in the pharmaceutical industry in Oncology with a strong background in Immuno-oncology market access, pricing, reimbursement or payer authority roles- Demonstrated experience supporting global pricing and access strategy development for Immuno-oncology assets, ideally during pre-launch or launch-phase planning.- Deep understanding of global healthcare systems across major markets and the ability to adapt strategies to market-specific requirements.- Proven ability to independently lead complex cross-functional market access initiatives and translate ambiguity into clear recommendations and actionable plans.- Fluent English communication, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process. We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. In cases of equal qualifications, such applicants will be given preferential consideration in the selection process.With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.comReady to contact us?If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team, Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or via mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.comRecruitment process:Step 1: Online application - The job posting is presumably online until November 19th, 2026. We reserve the right to take the posting offline beforehand. Applications up to November 12th, 2026 are guaranteed to be considered.Step 2: Virtual meeting in the period from end November till Mid of DecemberStep 3: On-site interviews beginning of January
